q: You want to dynamically update a text element whenever a reactive title string changes. Which directive should you use?
explain: The v-text directive sets the textContent of an element to the reactive value. This updates automatically while automatically escaping HTML characters for safety.

q: You are building a toggle switch that should completely remove or re-insert a heavy sidebar container in the DOM. Which directive achieves this?
explain: The v-if directive performs real conditional rendering by destroying and recreating the target elements in the DOM structure during toggles.

q: You need to attach a standard browser submit event listener to a form element and invoke a submitForm method. Which syntax is valid?
explain: The v-on directive binds native event listeners to DOM elements. It intercepts events and maps them directly to your specified methods or functions.

q: You are passing a live variable named themeColor down to a child component as an HTML attribute. Which shorthand syntax binds it?
explain: The colon symbol is the standard framework shorthand for v-bind. It lets you pass dynamic attributes and reactive javascript values directly to tags.

q: You need to intercept a click event on an anchor tag and prevent the browser from executing its default page refresh. Which modifier works?
explain: The prevent event modifier automatically invokes event.preventDefault() under the hood. This cancels the native browser behavior like navigating anchor tags.

q: You are creating a text input element that needs to continuously synchronize its value with a local text variable. Which directive handles this?
explain: The v-model directive provides automated two-way data binding. It updates the state on element inputs and updates the element value on state changes.

q: You want to render a recurring list of blog items on screen based on an items array in your state. Which loop directive handles this?
explain: The v-for directive loops through arrays or iterable objects. It uses a specific alias syntax to dynamically render blocks of HTML markup.

q: Your product list template uses v-for but your compiler produces warnings about missing tracked elements during list mutations. What attribute fixes this?
explain: The key attribute provides unique identity hints to the rendering engine. This allows the internal virtual DOM diffing engine to track and optimize item movements safely.

q: You need to reference an raw HTML string safely inside an empty span tag without displaying raw code to users. Which directive is used?
explain: The v-html directive modifies the element innerHTML property with your raw string contents. Use it cautiously to avoid malicious cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.

q: You are updating a numeric value inside a script setup block and want to log a message whenever that state changes. Which native utility handles this?
explain: The watch primitive observes specific reactive dependencies. When changes occur, it triggers an isolated callback function where custom logging or logic can run.

q: You are declaring a primitive string variable called username inside script setup and need it to maintain reactivity. Which function should wrap it?
explain: The ref function creates an observable reference holding primitive values or complex objects. It wraps your value in a reactive wrapper accessible via value properties.

q: You need to access a ref variable named count inside the javascript setup function to increment its value. How do you target its inner content?
explain: In javascript blocks, variables created with ref are reactive objects. You must use the value property to explicitly read or overwrite their wrapped data values.

q: You are initializing a structured object representing a form state and prefer not to deal with value properties in javascript. Which utility should wrap it?
explain: The reactive utility maps proxies onto complex javascript objects directly. This enables tracking property modifications transparently without using an intermediate value wrapper object.

q: You have a derived product value calculated from a base price and tax percentage that must be cached automatically. Which function should calculate it?
explain: Computed values create read-only reactive properties. They analyze their internal dependencies and cache the result, re-running only when referenced values are modified.

q: You need to execute an initial analytics fetch request as soon as your component has completed its real DOM mounting. Which hook handles this?
explain: The onMounted hook runs immediately after the component template nodes are instantiated and appended into the real web browser DOM tree.

q: You need to clean up an active browser interval timer before a component gets completely unmounted and destroyed. Which lifecycle hook is appropriate?
explain: The onUnmounted lifecycle hook fires after a component instance is entirely dismantled, making it the secure location to clean up side effects.

q: You want to transmit a read-only configuration string from a parent down to a nested child element. What component attribute type implements this?
explain: Props are custom attributes explicitly declared on components. They allow parents to feed one-way data downstream to children consistently.

q: Your child modal element needs to notify its immediate parent container that its close button was clicked. Which system handles this?
explain: The emit method allows child components to fire custom events. Parent elements listen to these events in templates to trigger local callback logic.

q: You want to declare a slot fallback element inside a custom button layout that shows up only if a parent component leaves the slot empty. How do you design this?
explain: Placing child nodes directly inside the slot tags creates default content. The browser displays this default text only if the parent component skips injecting dynamic templates.

q: You want to ensure that style rules inside your single file component do not bleed out and accidentally color elements in other views. What tag configuration guarantees this?
explain: The scoped attribute on style blocks instructs the compiler to append unique dataset attributes to internal markup, keeping rules safely confined to the current element.

q: You are setting up multi-page view paths within an application dashboard using modern routing libraries. Which component acts as the placeholder container?
explain: The RouterView element acts as a dynamic structural placeholder. The routing engine swap-renders matching route path components into this specific section on navigation.

q: You are creating navigation items in an application head element and need an alternative to standard anchor tags that prevents browser reloads. What should you use?
explain: The RouterLink component handles user navigation smoothly. It renders a valid anchor tag under the hood but blocks native reloads to swap views locally.

q: You want to create a global single source of truth store using Pinia for authentication metrics. Which initialization function defines this container?
explain: Pinia structures store definitions via the defineStore method. It takes a distinct unique key string along with an configuration object or setup function.

q: You are designing an interactive list where elements must appear or fade out using custom animations when structural toggles occur. What built-in tag wraps them?
explain: The built-in Transition element applies automated class sequences onto a wrapped element during entering and leaving state shifts.

q: You have thousands of users viewing a flat marketing page that renders static copy which never changes after initial mount. What directive halts updates here?
explain: The v-once directive tells the compiler to render an element block exactly once and skip all future reactive tracking updates entirely to save processing power.
